subject: Latency commitment addendum — measurement cadence & exceptions
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nimbusfin.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Costa <elena.costa@nimbusfin.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — request to tighten p95 and measurement cadence

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we finalize the commercial terms for the P0 integration, our infra team pushed back on the latency commitments in the draft SOW — specifically p95 and how you measure it. For production traffic we need clearer guarantees and a faster measurement cadence so we can rely on operational SLAs for our consumer-facing flows.

To be concrete, Nimbus is asking for:
- p50 <= 120 ms across the text-completion endpoint
- p95 <= 650 ms
- Measurement reported on a rolling 24-hour window (vs a multi-day aggregation)

We also need a short carveout definition for planned maintenance and large-scale bursts (e.g., holiday batch jobs). Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to those numbers and the 24-hour window, or propose alternative wording we can take to procurement?

Attaching a short note from our SRE with sample traffic patterns (see attached).

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Financial
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — request to tighten p95 and measurement cadence

Tom —

Appreciate the clear ask and the sample traffic. Short answer: we can get closer, but there are tradeoffs depending on model family, region, and burst profile. A few quick clarifications that will help us make a firm commitment: 

1) Which model(s) are you planning to serve at production? Large-chat models have different tail characteristics than smaller text-only models.
2) Is the 24-hour rolling window a hard requirement for SLA enforcement, or would you accept a 24-hour reporting window with a 7-day rolling eligibility for penalties?
3) Expected QPS and typical prompt length (token distribution) — the attached sample helps but a single-number QPS peak would be useful.

Ben and I will draft a short addendum that defines measurement (sampling cadence, client-side vs proxy), carveouts, and an optional phased target for the first 90 days. I’ve looped Aditya for observability implications.

I’ll follow up with a proposed addendum PDF by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, GTM Strategy — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-08T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: internal: Nimbus latency ask — quick notes

Lauren / team —

Notes from my side for the addendum draft:
- Our standard hosted baseline uses a 7-day rolling window with 1-minute sampling and a 5-minute aggregation bucket; we surface both daily and 7-day views.
- We can offer a 24-hour reporting window but need to distinguish reporting from liabilities. Suggest: 24-hour reporting for operational alerts + 7-day rolling window for penalty triggers (this reduces sensitivity to transient bursts).
- Proposed phase: first 30 days (onboarding) we commit to p50 <= 140ms / p95 <= 700ms, then post-stabilization (30–90d) we tighten to p50 <= 120ms / p95 <= 650ms, assuming token and QPS profiles match sample.
- Carveouts: scheduled maint with 4-hour advance notice; major-region failover; operator-initiated emergency patches; a single large-scale traffic anomaly per calendar month (with evidence).

Aditya — can you add a short paragraph on how we compute p95 (sample size, weighted percentiles, how early-truncation is handled)? Rishi — include legal phrasing for force majeure and measurement dispute escalation to the addendum.

Ben
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nimbusfin.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Costa <elena.costa@nimbusfin.com>, Procurement <procure@nimbusfin.com>
Date: 2027-09-09T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — request to tighten p95 and measurement cadence

Lauren/Ben —

Thanks for the quick internal alignment. A few clarifications from our side:
- We will be serving the standard text-completion endpoint (inference-only) backed by a mid-sized decoder model (token lengths average 120–180).
- Peak QPS is expected to be ~30 requests/s initially, spiking to 120 requests/s during promotions.
- For liability, procurement prefers a clear 24-hour enforcement window because our ops run daily reconciliation against that metric. If you cannot provide that, we can accept the phased approach but need an explicit calendar for the tightening step.

We can be flexible on a single large-scale anomaly carveout, but the scheduled maintenance windows should be limited to 2 hours and require 24-hour notice (our compliance team is strict).

Tom
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Elena Costa <elena.costa@nimbusfin.com>
Date: 2027-09-10T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — request to tighten p95 and measurement cadence

Tom / Elena —

Attached is a proposed addendum (Nimbus_Redwood_SLO_Addendum_v1.pdf) that reflects the compromise we discussed:
- Measurement definitions: 1-minute sampling; 24-hour reporting dashboard available; enforcement (liability) calculated on a 7-day rolling window with a 24-hour emergency-trigger clause (see section 2.3).
- Phased commitments: onboarding (0–30 days) p50 <= 140 ms / p95 <= 700 ms; stabilization (31–90 days) p50 <= 120 ms / p95 <= 650 ms; steady-state (post-90 days) optional renegotiation based on actual token/QPS profile.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance capped at 2 hours with 24-hour notice; single-month major-anomaly carveout; regional failover allowances.
- Measurement disputes: we publish raw sampled metrics and a CSV (measurement-samples.csv) on request within 48 hours; disputes escalate to a joint SRE review panel.

If that alignment looks good, we’ll send a final redline-ready PDF for procurement and add the addendum to the primary MSA. I’ve included explicit HubSpot deal references and a DocuSign template in the draft.

Quick ask for Nimbus procurement: confirm whether the 7-day enforcement clause is a deal-breaker. If so, I’ll pull legal to propose a revenue-at-risk cap instead of a full 24-hour enforcement window.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, GTM Strategy — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Nimbus_Redwood_SLO_Addendum_v1.pdf (defines metrics, examples, and escalation cadence)
Attachment: measurement-samples.csv (redwood-sampled-metrics snippet)
From: Elena Costa <elena.costa@nimbusfin.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@nimbusfin.com>
Date: 2027-09-10T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — request to tighten p95 and measurement cadence

Lauren —

Thank you for the draft addendum and the phased path. Procurement has reviewed and the 7-day enforcement approach is acceptable provided there is a 24-hour reporting dashboard and the ability to trigger an emergency 24-hour enforcement window with documented evidence. That aligns with our operational reconciliation cadence.

Next steps from Nimbus:
1) Procurement will run the redline — I’ll expect it back by Thursday EOD.
2) We’ll request the raw CSV sample for a 7-day period to sanity-check the metrics before signature.
3) Once redlines are completed, we’ll route the addendum to legal and aim for signature the week after.

Please include the HubSpot deal id (NIM-90827) on the final PDF.

Elena Costa
Head of Compliance, Nimbus Financial
Procurement: procure@nimbusfin.com
